tip.general: GENERAL — the main switch: cuts all the power to the board.
tip.diff: RCD / residual-current device: protects PEOPLE — it trips if it detects current leaking to earth (e.g. a bare wire someone touches).
tip.test: RCD test button: press it to simulate a leak and check the RCD trips. Worth testing now and then.
tip.mcb: MCB / circuit breaker: protects the CABLE — it trips on overload or short-circuit.
tip.dimmerChan: Dimmer channel — one dimmable output, protected by its breaker.
tip.directos: DIRECTOS: constant (un-dimmed) power. LED / DMX fixtures plug here — NEVER into a dimmer or they break.
tip.canales: Dimmer channel outputs (1-36) — the dimmers' regulated outputs.
tip.circuitos: Stage circuits (1-48): the fixed wiring to the bars. Patch one to a dimmer channel with a jumper to control it.
tip.dimmerScreen: Dimmer display — shows the channel / DMX info once the rack is powered on.

help.title: How does the board work?
help.intro: The path: mains → GENERAL → split into lines (dimmers, force/directs, sound, emergency) → protections → fixtures.

general.b: The master key: gives or cuts power to the WHOLE board. Lever up = on.

diff.b: Protects PEOPLE: it trips if it detects current leaking to earth (a bare wire someone touches, damp…), cutting in milliseconds. The blue button is TEST: it simulates a leak to check the RCD trips; if it does not trip when pressed, it is faulty.

mcb.b: Protects the CABLE: it trips on overload (more power than the cable can take) or short-circuit (two wires touching). It has 1, 2 or 4 levers depending on the poles.

dimmer.b: Dims the INTENSITY of analog lights: it takes DMX from the Quartz and lets more or less voltage through to the lamp. 3 units × 12 = 36 channels. Its little screen lights up when the rack has power.

directos.b: Constant (un-dimmed) power outlets. LED / DMX fixtures plug in here — they dim themselves internally. ⚠️ Never into a dimmer or they break.

patch.b: The CIRCUITOS (1-48) are the fixed wiring to the stage bars; the CANALES DE DIMMERS (1-36) are the dimmers regulated outputs. A jumper joins circuit → dimmer channel and decides which dimmer controls each fixture. That number is its DMX address (circuit 8 → dimmer 1 = DMX 1).

rule.b: Analog → ALWAYS to a dimmer (its DMX address is the dimmer channel). LED / DMX → ALWAYS to directos, and the DMX address is set on the fixture itself.
